content:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's KV "aging policy" change we saw repeated 50-150ms tail spikes on a subset of hosts during bursty traffic.

oliver: ugh, saw one alert around 03:12. which policy was toggled? LRU->FIFO or something hybrid?

maria: We flipped default to FIFO-prefactor (experiment) on the 03:00 deploy to reduce reinsert churn.

cheng: can you paste the alert histogram? wondering if it's correlated with sequence length / batching.

maria: pasted below. note the sawtooth pattern — latency climbs after each sustained burst then relaxes.

maria: ```
host-a 03:10-03:30 p95: 12ms -> 65ms -> 20ms -> 72ms (repeats)
host-b 03:10-03:30 p95: 10ms -> 48ms -> 18ms -> 50ms
request rate: 1200rps burst windows ~30s
kv-evicts/sec: spikes from 200->1500 during ramps
```

ryan: interesting. KV evicts/sec jump aligns with latency. Did FIFO increase full-page scans or cause reinsert storms?

maria: profile attached (pprof CPU samples) — main hotspots in kv_pager::reclaim and kv_cache::lookup miss path.

sara: @cheng can you run a quick profiler on a repro node and share flamegraph? I want to see if we stall on copying pages vs mutex contention.

cheng: ran sampling for 60s during a synthetic sawtooth. quick notes:
- heavy loop in `evict_scan()` when reclaiming contiguous slots
- mutex contention on `kv_buckets_lock` during concurrent reinsert
- increased memcopies while compacting fragmented slabs

cheng: flame snippet: `evict_scan` 35%, `reinsert` 18%, `copy_kv_page` 12%, user-request handlers ~8%

oliver: sounds like FIFO causes long-running scan/compact phases that block lookups. LRU spreads evictions so scans are less contiguous.

maria: also noticed cache-reuse misses after bursts — items needed again shortly after eviction, causing recompute and extra KV allocations. reuse ratio drops from 0.78 -> 0.42 during spikes.

ryan: that will amplify latency due to model kernel warmup + KV restore. Batching heuristics might be amplifying this too: large batches during ramp mean longer KV lifetime expectations.

maria: quick repro command we used:
```bash
# sawtooth load using wrk2
wrk2 -t8 -c400 -d120s -R1200 --latency http://host-a:8080/generate?model=redwood-micro
# config: kv.aging_policy=fifo-prefactor, kv.page_size=64mb, batching.max_batch_tokens=1024
```

sara: ops note: infra-bot rolled back the FIFO-prefactor on 03:45 to LRU-default. early rollbacks removed most tail spikes.

infra-bot: rollback completed: deploy 2026-03-17T03:45:21Z -> reverted kv.aging_policy to lru-default on fleet=blue, status=success

maria: after rollback p95 stabilized ~12-20ms, evicts/sec flattened ~120-240 range.

cheng: hypothesis: FIFO-prefactor increases locality for long-lived keys but under bursty sawtooth load it creates fragmentation and long compaction windows which block lookups. Also reinsert churn creates mutex hot path.

oliver: possible mitigations:
- make evict_scan incremental (work-slicing) to avoid long pauses
- use per-shard locks to limit contention
- tune fifo-prefactor threshold so hot items are protected by short TTL-based grace
- add async reinsert to avoid holding request path locks

maria: I sketched a small patch that does incremental scanning + backoff when reuse ratio < 0.5. local tests reduced p95 spike magnitude by ~3x. sharing PR soon: github.com/redwood/infra/pulls/1256

ryan: also run a variant with smaller page_size (32mb) and measure fragmentation — might reduce copy cost during compact.

maria: noted. will run experiments with page_size and batching.max_batch_tokens separately to isolate kernel vs batching effects.

sara: thanks all. next steps: 1) monitor canary for a day, 2) land incremental-scan patch behind feature flag, 3) add synthetic sawtooth job to perf-suite for regression catch.

oliver: also add a perf test that toggles LRU/FIFO under varying burst patterns so we don't get surprised again.

maria: agreed. will follow up with PR and perf runs. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
